docs.title: Frameworks
docs.text:
<quran-madina-html> is a standard web component, so it works in any framework that renders HTML. Three frameworks get a dedicated package, because they can't use the tag directly or gain a lot from one:

  • React: @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react, a component that loads the library for you, for React on the web and, through Capacitor, on iOS and Android.
  • React Native: @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native, a component that shows the tag in a WebView on iOS and Android, sized to the text, online or offline.
  • Flutter: quran_madina_flutter, a widget for Android, iOS, macOS and the web.

The others use the tag as it is, with a line or two of setup:

Framework Setup Page Vue, Nuxt mark the tag as a custom element in the compiler options Vue Angular CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA on the component Angular Svelte, SvelteKit none Svelte Astro load the script with is:inline Astro SolidJS, Preact, Lit, Alpine, plain JavaScript none: write the tag, or create it with document.createElement HTML

Next.js is React: use the React component in a client component ("use client"). WordPress sites use the plugin, with a block and a shortcode.

docs.title: Setting values from code
docs.text: Every attribute is also a property: tag.aya = 256 is the same as tag.setAttribute("aya", "256"), and either re-renders the tag. true sets an empty attribute, and null or false removes it. Frameworks that pass values as properties (Vue, Svelte, Angular's [aya]) rely on this, which needs library 2.1.2 or later.

docs.title: Angular
docs.text: Angular renders <quran-madina-html> once a component allows custom elements, and the page loads the library's script.

docs.title: 1. Load the library
docs.text:
In src/index.html, inside <head>:

<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2"></script>

Page-wide options (print, size, self-hosting) go on this tag: see Script options.

docs.title: 2. Allow the custom element
docs.text:
Add CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA to each component that uses the tag (or to its NgModule):

import { Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA } from "@angular/core";

@Component({
  selector: "app-verse",
  standalone: true,
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  template: `
    <quran-madina-html sura="2" [attr.aya]="aya" highlight="5-8" headless></quran-madina-html>
    <button (click)="aya = aya + 1">Next verse</button>
  `,
})
export class VerseComponent {
  aya = 255;
}

Without the schema, the template fails to compile: "'quran-madina-html' is not a known element".

docs.title: 3. Bind values
docs.text:
Bind with [attr.name], which sets the attribute; the tag re-renders when it changes:

<quran-madina-html [attr.sura]="sura" [attr.aya]="aya" [attr.letters]="letters"></quran-madina-html>

From library 2.1.2, plain property bindings ([aya]="aya") work too. Every option is listed in Tag attributes.

docs.title: Offline
docs.text:
Copy the library into the app with the bundler that ships with the React wrapper, version 2.1.2 or later (it doesn't need React), into a folder Angular serves, such as public/ (Angular 17+) or src/assets/:

npx -p @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react quran-madina-bundle --layouts 1441H --out public/quran-madina

Then load it from there:

<script src="/quran-madina/dist/quran-madina-html.js" data-cdn="/quran-madina/"></script>

See Self-hosting and offline.

docs.title: Astro
docs.text: In Astro the tag is plain HTML: it works in .astro pages and layouts with no integration.

docs.title: 1. Load the library
docs.text:
In your layout's <head>. is:inline keeps Astro from bundling the script, which the library needs, since it reads its options from its own <script> tag:

<script is:inline src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2"></script>

Page-wide options (print, size, self-hosting) go on this tag: see Script options.

docs.title: 2. Use it
docs.text:
---
const verse = { sura: 2, aya: 255 };
---
<quran-madina-html sura={verse.sura} aya={verse.aya} highlight="5-8" headless></quran-madina-html>

Values in {...} are written as attributes when the page is built, so this works on static and server-rendered pages alike. Every option is listed in Tag attributes.

Inside a React, Vue or Svelte island, follow that framework's page.

docs.title: Offline
docs.text:
Copy the library into public/ with the bundler that ships with the React wrapper, version 2.1.2 or later (it doesn't need React):

npx -p @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react quran-madina-bundle --layouts 1441H

Then load it from there:

<script is:inline src="/quran-madina/dist/quran-madina-html.js" data-cdn="/quran-madina/"></script>

See Self-hosting and offline.

docs.title: Flutter
docs.text:
quran_madina_flutter is a widget that wraps the <quran-madina-html> tag. It has the same options as the tag and the React component, and is released together with the library, under the same version number.

Try it

The example app, built for the web, runs live at https://tarekeldeeb.github.io/quran-madina-html/flutter/.

import 'package:quran_madina_flutter/quran_madina_flutter.dart';

QuranMadinaFlutter(page: 106)                                  // a full page
QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 2, aya: '255')                        // a verse
QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '1', words: '1:2')            // some words
QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 2, aya: '255', highlight: '5-8', error: '1')
QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '2-4', letters: '1:3, 4:3-5 emerald blink')
QuranMadinaFlutter(page: 50, layout: 'IndoPak', fontSize: 22)
QuranMadinaFlutter(page: 106, bundled: true)                   // offline, from the app's assets

The widget sizes itself to the rendered text, so it fits in a ListView or Column. You can also pass height to fix it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dependencies:
  quran_madina_flutter: ^2.1.0

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text:
Platform How it renders Android The system WebView (via webview_flutter) iOS, macOS WKWebView, the engine Safari uses (via webview_flutter) Web No WebView: the <quran-madina-html> tag goes straight into the page

Each widget on Android, iOS and macOS is its own WebView, so use one or a few per screen. For a long passage, render it in one widget (sura: 2, aya: '1-20') rather than one widget per verse.

On the web, the library reads layout, fontSize and its URLs once for the whole page, so the first widget's values apply to every widget. The translate links open in a new browser tab. If your web/index.html already loads the library script, the widget uses it.

docs.title: Online or offline
docs.text:
By default the library, its databases and fonts load from unpkg, so the app needs internet access. On Android, the release build needs the INTERNET permission.

To work offline, copy the library into your app once, from the app's folder:

dart run quran_madina_flutter:bundle                     # the 1441H layout (about 4 MB)
dart run quran_madina_flutter:bundle --layouts 1441H,IndoPak   # about 4 MB per layout

The command writes assets/quran_madina/ and prints the asset folders to add to your pubspec.yaml:

flutter:
  assets:
    - assets/quran_madina/assets/db/v2/
    - assets/quran_madina/assets/db/v2/Madina-1441H/
    - assets/quran_madina/assets/img/
    - assets/quran_madina/dist/

Then pass bundled: true:

QuranMadinaFlutter(page: 106, bundled: true)

Run the command again after upgrading this package, so the files match its version. It downloads the matching library version from npm. --version picks another version, and --from <folder> copies from a built checkout of quran-madina-html instead.

On the web, the bundled files are served with the app's own assets, with no other setup.

On Android, iOS and macOS, a WebView can't read Flutter assets directly, so the widget serves them to it from a small local server on 127.0.0.1. Allow that connection once per platform:

Android: add android/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:

<network-security-config>
  <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true">
    <domain includeSubdomains="false">127.0.0.1</domain>
  </domain-config>
</network-security-config>

Point to it in AndroidManifest.xml, and keep the INTERNET permission. The local server needs it, even offline.

<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/>
<application android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config" ...>

iOS and macOS: in Info.plist:

<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
  <key>NSAllowsLocalNetworking</key>
  <true/>
</dict>

On macOS, also add com.apple.security.network.server and com.apple.security.network.client to macos/Runner/DebugProfile.entitlements and Release.entitlements.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Type Description page int Full Mushaf page (1–604; IndoPak 1–610). Wins over sura/aya. sura, aya int, String Sura (1–114) and aya or range, e.g. '255', '8-10'. words String 1-based word range, e.g. '1:2', '3-10', '5'. highlight String Word range marked soft yellow. error String Word range marked soft red (wins over highlight). letters String Letters to emphasise inside words: '1:3 crimson, 4:3-5 emerald blink'. Each group is word:letters, then an optional colour (crimson by default), then an optional blink. headless bool Drop the header (sura name, copy/translate) and show only the text. quotes String 'no' drops the quote marks around inline renders. inline String 'no' forces the multiline layout. notitle bool With words crossing into a new sura: hide its name, keep the frame. layout String '1441H' (default), '1405H' or 'IndoPak'. fontSize num Font size in logical pixels (default 16). textColor String CSS colour of the text, e.g. '#ece6d6' for a dark theme. Highlight, error and letter colours adapt to it. backgroundColor String CSS colour behind the text (default transparent). height double Fixed height instead of sizing to the text. bundled bool Load everything from the app's assets (see above) instead of unpkg. onOpenUrl void Function(String) Called with links the library opens: the translate buttons, to quran.com. Open them with url_launcher. By default they are ignored. On the web, the browser opens them. src, cdn String Library script URL and asset base URL (default: unpkg, latest 2.x). Use these to load the library from your own server.

Changing page, sura, aya, words, highlight, error, letters or the other tag options re-renders in place. Changing layout, fontSize, textColor, backgroundColor, bundled, src or cdn reloads the WebView.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The example app has an online/offline switch. Its web build runs live at https://tarekeldeeb.github.io/quran-madina-html/flutter/.

docs.title: React Native
docs.text: @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native shows the <quran-madina-html> tag in a react-native-webview WebView, sized to the text, on iOS and Android. It takes the same options as the React component and the Flutter widget, and can work offline.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
npm install @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native react-native-webview
cd ios && pod install    # bare React Native on iOS

With Expo: npx expo install @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native react-native-webview. It works in Expo Go online; offline needs a development build (see Offline).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import QuranMadinaNative from "@tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native";

<QuranMadinaNative sura={2} aya="255" />                          {/* a verse */}
<QuranMadinaNative page={106} headless />                         {/* a full page */}
<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya={1} words="1:2" />                {/* some words */}
<QuranMadinaNative sura={2} aya="255" highlight="5-8" error="1" />
<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya="2-4" letters="1:3, 4:3-5 emerald blink" />
<QuranMadinaNative page={50} layout="IndoPak" fontSize={22} />
<QuranMadinaNative page={106} bundled />                          {/* offline */}

The component takes the height of the rendered text, so it fits in a ScrollView or FlatList. Each one is its own WebView: for a long passage, render it in one component (sura={2} aya="1-20") rather than one per verse.

docs.title: Props
docs.text:
Prop Type Description page number | string A full page, 1–604 (IndoPak 1–610). Wins over sura/aya. sura, aya number | string Sura 1–114, and a verse or range: 255, "8-10". words string Only these words: "1:2", "3-10". See Selecting words. highlight string Words marked soft yellow, e.g. "5-8". error string Words marked soft red; wins over highlight. letters string Letters to emphasise, e.g. "1:3, 4:3-5 emerald blink". See Emphasising letters. headless boolean Only the Quran text, without the header. notitle boolean Hide the name of a sura a words selection crosses into. quotes string "no" drops the quote marks around inline renders. inline string "no" forces the multiline layout. layout string "1441H" (default), "1405H" or "IndoPak". Per component. fontSize number Size in points, default 16. textColor string CSS colour of the text, e.g. "#ece6d6" on a dark screen. Mark colours adapt to it. backgroundColor string CSS colour behind the text (default transparent). height number A fixed height instead of the text's. bundled boolean | string Load the library from the app instead of unpkg (see Offline). onOpenUrl (url) => void Links the library opens: the translate buttons, to quran.com. Default: Linking.openURL. src, cdn string Library script URL and file base URL (default: unpkg, latest 2.x). style ViewStyle Style of the outer view. webViewProps object Extra props for the WebView.

Changing page, sura, aya, words, highlight, error, letters or the other tag options updates the text in place. Changing layout, fontSize, the colours, bundled, src or cdn reloads the WebView.

docs.title: Offline
docs.text:
By default the library, its texts and fonts load from unpkg. To work offline, copy them into the app once, from the app's folder:

npx quran-madina-native-bundle                            # the 1441H layout (about 4 MB)
npx quran-madina-native-bundle --layouts 1441H,IndoPak    # about 4 MB per layout

It writes android/app/src/main/assets/quran-madina/ and ios/quran-madina/, for the platform folders your app has, with the library and the page the WebView opens.

iOS, once: in Xcode, drag the ios/quran-madina folder onto the project, choose Create folder references (it shows as a blue folder), and tick your app target. Android needs nothing more.

Then pass bundled:

<QuranMadinaNative page={106} bundled />
Option Default Description --layouts 1441H The prints to include: 1441H, 1405H, IndoPak, comma-separated. --version this package's version The quran-madina-html version to copy from npm. --from Copy from a built checkout of quran-madina-html instead of npm. --android, --ios the folders above Write somewhere else; then pass that folder's URL as bundled.

Run the command again after upgrading this package, so the files match its version.

Expo: offline needs native folders, so use a development build: run npx expo prebuild, then the command above (and the iOS step). Expo Go can't include them; use the online mode there.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The library loads in the WebView, so the app needs internet access unless it's bundled.
  • Text colour: the WebView doesn't inherit your app's styles. Pass textColor (and backgroundColor) for dark screens; the library then picks its dark-screen shades for marks and letters.
  • React Native for Web isn't supported (the WebView doesn't run there); on the web, use the React component.

docs.title: React
docs.text:
@tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react is a small component around the <quran-madina-html> tag. The same component runs on the web and, inside a Capacitor app, on iOS and Android.

The library itself isn't bundled: the component adds its <script> when it first mounts, because the library reads its options from its own script tag. react is a peer dependency.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: npm install @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react react

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import QuranMadinaHtml from "@tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <div dir="rtl">
      <QuranMadinaHtml page={106} layout="1441H" />                {/* a full page */}
      <QuranMadinaHtml sura={2} aya="8-10" />                      {/* verses */}
      <QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya={1} words="1:2" />             {/* some words */}
      <QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya={1} words="1-14" error="10-13" />
      <QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya="2-4" letters="1:3, 4:3-5 emerald blink" />
      <QuranMadinaHtml sura={2} aya="13-14" headless />            {/* no header */}
      <QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya={3} quotes="no" />             {/* inline, no quote marks */}
      <QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya={3} inline="no" />             {/* force the multiline layout */}
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: Props
docs.text:
Prop Type Notes page number | string Full page, 1–604 (IndoPak 1–610). Wins over sura/aya. sura number | string Sura 1–114, with aya. aya number | string Verse or range, e.g. "8-10". words string Word range: "1:2", "3-10", or one number. See Selecting words. highlight string Word range marked soft yellow, e.g. "5-8". error string Word range marked soft red. letters string Letters to emphasise, e.g. "1:3 crimson, 4:3-5 emerald blink". See Emphasising letters. headless boolean Drop the header. notitle boolean Hide the name of a sura a words selection crosses into. quotes string "no" drops the quote marks around inline renders. inline string "no" forces the multiline layout. layout string 1441H (default), 1405H or IndoPak. fontSize number | string Size in px, default 16. src string Library script URL. Default: unpkg, latest. cdn string Base URL of the library's files. Default: unpkg. bundled boolean | string Load the app's own copy of the library, made by npx quran-madina-bundle (see Offline). true loads it from /quran-madina/; a string is the URL the copy is served at. Overrides src and cdn. font, name string Ignored since 2.0 (the library logs a warning).

Page-wide options

layout, fontSize, src, cdn and bundled configure the one library instance on the page. Only the first <QuranMadinaHtml> to mount sets them; later values are ignored.

docs.title: Why cdn is set
docs.text:
Without data-cdn, the library loads its files from ../ on any localhost page (see the localhost rule). A React dev server and a Capacitor app both run on localhost, so the component always sets cdn, to unpkg by default. To use your own copy:

<QuranMadinaHtml page={1} cdn="https://my.cdn.example/quran-madina-html/" />

docs.title: iOS and Android with Capacitor
docs.text:
Capacitor wraps your React web build in a native app with a WebView, so the same component runs on the phone:

npm install @capacitor/core @capacitor/cli
npx cap init "My Quran App" com.example.quran --web-dir=dist
npm run build
npx cap add ios
npx cap add android
npx cap copy
npx cap open ios        # Xcode
npx cap open android    # Android Studio

docs.title: Offline
docs.text:
By default the library, its databases and fonts load from unpkg. To work offline, copy them into your app once, from the app's folder:

npx quran-madina-bundle                            # the 1441H layout (about 4 MB)
npx quran-madina-bundle --layouts 1441H,IndoPak    # about 4 MB per layout

The command writes public/quran-madina/, which Vite, Create React App and Next.js serve as /quran-madina/, and Capacitor copies into the app with the rest of the build. Then pass bundled:

<QuranMadinaHtml page={106} bundled />
Option Default Description --layouts 1441H The prints to include: 1441H, 1405H, IndoPak, comma-separated. --out public/quran-madina Where to write the files. --version this package's version The quran-madina-html version to copy from npm. --from Copy from a built checkout of quran-madina-html instead of npm.

If the folder is served somewhere else (a different --out, or an app under a sub-path), pass that URL instead: bundled="/my-app/quran-madina/".

Run the command again after upgrading this package, so the files match its version. It replaces the whole folder, so only the layouts you list stay.

docs.title: React Native
docs.text: Not supported. React Native has no HTML or CSS, so the tag can't run there. Use Capacitor, or a WebView component.

docs.title: Svelte
docs.text: Svelte renders <quran-madina-html> as it is; there's nothing to configure. The page only needs the library's script.

docs.title: 1. Load the library
docs.text:
Inside <head> of src/app.html (SvelteKit) or index.html (Vite):

<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2"></script>

Page-wide options (print, size, self-hosting) go on this tag: see Script options.

docs.title: 2. Use it
docs.text:
<script>
  let aya = $state(255);
</script>

<quran-madina-html sura="2" aya={aya} highlight="5-8" headless></quran-madina-html>
<button onclick={() => aya++}>Next verse</button>

Bound values update the render when they change. With SvelteKit, the tag is rendered on the server as plain HTML and comes to life in the browser. Every option is listed in Tag attributes.

Library 2.1.2 and later

In the browser, Svelte passes {...} values to custom elements as properties, which the tag turns into attributes from 2.1.2. Older versions only see values written as plain text (aya="255").

docs.title: Offline
docs.text:
Copy the library into static/ (SvelteKit) or public/ (Vite) with the bundler that ships with the React wrapper, version 2.1.2 or later (it doesn't need React):

npx -p @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react quran-madina-bundle --layouts 1441H --out static/quran-madina

Then load it from there:

<script src="/quran-madina/dist/quran-madina-html.js" data-cdn="/quran-madina/"></script>

See Self-hosting and offline.

docs.title: Vue
docs.text: Vue renders <quran-madina-html> like any element. It only needs to know the tag isn't a Vue component, and the page needs the library's script.

docs.title: 1. Load the library
docs.text:
In index.html, inside <head>:

<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2"></script>

Page-wide options (print, size, self-hosting) go on this tag: see Script options.

docs.title: 2. Tell Vue it's a custom element
docs.text:
With Vite, in vite.config.js:

import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import vue from "@vitejs/plugin-vue";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    vue({
      template: {
        compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag === "quran-madina-html" },
      },
    }),
  ],
});

Without this, Vue logs "Failed to resolve component: quran-madina-html" and still renders it. Nuxt takes the same option under vue.compilerOptions in nuxt.config.ts.

docs.title: 3. Use it
docs.text:
<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue";
const aya = ref(255);
</script>

<template>
  <quran-madina-html sura="2" :aya="aya" highlight="5-8" headless></quran-madina-html>
  <button @click="aya++">Next verse</button>
</template>

Bound values update the render when they change. Every option is listed in Tag attributes.

Library 2.1.2 and later

Vue passes bound values to custom elements as properties. The tag turns those into attributes from 2.1.2. With an older version, bind them as attributes instead: :aya.attr="aya".

docs.title: Offline
docs.text:
Copy the library into public/ with the bundler that ships with the React wrapper, version 2.1.2 or later (it doesn't need React):

npx -p @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react quran-madina-bundle --layouts 1441H

Then load it from there:

<script src="/quran-madina/dist/quran-madina-html.js" data-cdn="/quran-madina/"></script>

See Self-hosting and offline.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
quran-madina-html is a web component: a script that defines the <quran-madina-html> tag. Pick the way you build your app:

You build with Use Page Plain HTML, or any web framework the script and the tag HTML React (web, or iOS/Android through Capacitor) @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react React React Native (iOS, Android, Expo) @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native React Native Flutter (Android, iOS, macOS, web) quran_madina_flutter Flutter Vue, Angular, Svelte, Astro the script and the tag, with a line of setup Frameworks WordPress (no code) the Quran Madina Html plugin: a block and a shortcode WordPress

All three render the same way and take the same options, released together with the same version number.

docs.title: Flutter
docs.text:
dependencies:
  quran_madina_flutter: ^2.1.0

import 'package:quran_madina_flutter/quran_madina_flutter.dart';

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 2, aya: '255')

The widget sizes itself to the text, so it fits in a ListView or Column. It runs on Android, iOS and macOS (in the platform's WebView) and on the web (straight in the page), and can work offline from the app's own assets.

See Flutter for every option and the offline setup, and the live web example.

docs.title: Add the script
docs.text:
Load the library once, in the page's <head>:

<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2"></script>

Or install it from npm and serve the files yourself (see Self-hosting and offline):

npm install quran-madina-html

docs.title: Add a tag
docs.text:
Put a tag wherever the text should appear:

<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="1-7"></quran-madina-html>

A selection that fits on one line renders inline, inside your text, between quote marks: the verse sits in this sentence.

the verse <quran-madina-html sura="112" aya="1"></quran-madina-html> sits in this sentence.

docs.title: Choose the print and the size
docs.text:
Options for the whole page go on the script tag:

<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2" data-layout="1405H" data-font-size="22"></script>

See Layouts and sizes and Script options.

docs.title: Upgrading from 1.x
docs.text: Version 2 is a drop-in replacement: existing tags render unchanged. The 1.x font options (data-font, data-name) are ignored, with a console warning. To keep the 1.x renderer, pin quran-madina-html@1. The old documentation is under Version 1.x.

docs.title: React Native
docs.text:
npm install @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native react-native-webview

import QuranMadinaNative from "@tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react-native";

<QuranMadinaNative sura={2} aya="255" />

It shows the text in a WebView on iOS and Android, sized to the text, with the same options as the React component. For offline use, npx quran-madina-native-bundle copies the library into the app and bundled loads it from there.

See React Native for every prop, the offline setup and Expo.

docs.title: React
docs.text:
npm install @tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react react

import QuranMadinaHtml from "@tarekeldeeb/quran-madina-react";

export default function App() {
  return <QuranMadinaHtml sura={2} aya="255" />;
}

The component loads the library for you, so there is no script tag to add. Props take the same names as the tag's attributes, plus layout and fontSize for the page-wide options.

For offline use, npx quran-madina-bundle copies the library into your app and bundled loads it from there. The same component runs on iOS and Android inside a Capacitor app. See React for every prop and the mobile guide.

docs.title: WordPress
docs.text: The Quran Madina Html plugin adds a Quran block and a [quran] shortcode to any WordPress site. No code needed.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Download the plugin: quran-madina-html-wordpress.zip (from the latest GitHub release).
  2. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin, choose the zip, and Install Now.
  3. Activate it.

It needs WordPress 6.3 or later and PHP 7.4 or later.

docs.title: The Quran block
docs.text:
Add a Quran block (search for "Quran" or "قرآن" in the block inserter). Set it in the block sidebar:

Setting Example Shows Page 50 a whole page; leave empty to show verses Sura and Verses 2 and 255, or 2 and 8-10 those verses Only these words 1-5 only some words, counted from the first verse Highlight 5-8 words marked yellow Mistake 3 words marked red Letters 1:3, 4:3-5 emerald blink emphasised letters (format) Hide the header on only the Quran text, without the sura name, copy and translate

The text shows live in the editor as you change them.

docs.title: The shortcode
docs.text:
In any post, page or text widget:

[quran sura="2" aya="255"]
[quran page="1"]
[quran sura="2" aya="255" highlight="5-8" error="1"]
[quran sura="1" aya="2-4" letters="1:3, 4:3-5 emerald blink"]
[quran sura="1" aya="1" words="1-2"]
[quran sura="5" aya="1-2" headless="true"]

It takes every tag attribute: page, sura, aya, words, highlight, error, letters, headless, notitle, quotes, inline. A verse that fits on one line shows inline, inside the sentence:

[quran_madina ...] works too, in case another plugin already uses [quran].

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Under Settings → Quran Madina:

  • Print: the 1441H or 1405H Madina Mushaf, or the 15-line IndoPak. One print for the whole site.
  • Font size: in pixels, 16 by default.
  • Load the library from: unpkg.com (the default, nothing to set up), or this site.

docs.title: Without outside requests
docs.text:
To load nothing from unpkg.com (for privacy, or a site that must work on a closed network):

  1. Under Settings → Quran Madina, click Copy to this site. It downloads the library, its texts and fonts for all three prints (about 11 MB) into your uploads folder, once.
  2. Choose This site under "Load the library from", and Save.

After a plugin update, copy it again: each plugin version loads its own library version. Until you do, pages load from unpkg.com, and the settings page says so.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The library loads only on pages that show Quran text.
  • Light and dark themes are detected from your theme's text colour; see Styling and dark mode. Your theme's CSS can change the colours with the custom properties.
  • Caching and optimisation plugins: exclude the quran-madina-html script from "combine" or "defer" options if the text doesn't appear. The library reads its settings from its own script tag.
  • Uninstalling the plugin removes its settings and the copied library.

docs.title: License
docs.text: The plugin is dual licensed: GPLv2 or later, or the "Waqf" General Public License 2.0, at your choice (see LICENSE.txt in the plugin folder). The GPL option is for WordPress, whose plugins must be GPL compatible. The library the plugin loads, and the rest of this project, stay under the Waqf General Public License 2.0; the fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

docs.title: Guide
docs.text:
How to show what you need, one topic per page:

  • Pages and verses: a full page, a verse range, with or without the header.
  • Layouts and sizes: the three prints, and any font size.
  • Selecting words: show only some words, across verses and suras.
  • Highlighting words: mark words in yellow or red.
  • Emphasising letters: colour single letters inside words, optionally blinking.
  • Styling and dark mode: colours, dark pages, printing.
  • Self-hosting and offline: serve the files yourself, or bundle them in an app.

docs.title: Highlighting words
docs.text:
highlight marks words in soft yellow, and error in soft red, on top of whatever is shown. They take the same range format as words.

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="2" aya="255" highlight="5-8" error="1"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={2} aya="255" highlight="5-8" error="1" />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={2} aya="255" highlight="5-8" error="1" />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 2, aya: '255', highlight: '5-8', error: '1')

docs.title: What the numbers count
docs.text:
They work in every kind of render:

Render Word 1 is sura + aya the verse's first word with words the same word as in words (the selection's own numbering) a full page the first word of the page's first verse HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="7" words="1-14" highlight="10-13" error="1-2"></quran-madina-html>
<quran-madina-html page="2" error="1-4"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya="7" words="1-14" highlight="10-13" error="1-2" />
<QuranMadinaHtml page={2} error="1-4" />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya="7" words="1-14" highlight="10-13" error="1-2" />
<QuranMadinaNative page={2} error="1-4" />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '7', words: '1-14', highlight: '10-13', error: '1-2'),
QuranMadinaFlutter(page: 2, error: '1-4'),

A range must fall inside what is shown. One that doesn't, or that is malformed, is ignored with a console message; the text still renders. Where highlight and error overlap, error wins.

A basmala shown as the ﷽ ligature is split into its four words when a range marks only some of them.

docs.title: Colours
docs.text: The colours come from CSS custom properties, and switch to darker pairs with white text on dark pages automatically. See Styling and dark mode.

docs.title: Three prints
docs.text:
The script tag's data-layout picks the print. It applies to every tag on the page.

1441H (default)New Madina Mushaf 1405HOld Madina Mushaf IndoPak15-line IndoPak HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2" data-layout="IndoPak"></script>

{/* layout and fontSize apply to the whole page: set them on the first component */}
<QuranMadinaHtml layout="IndoPak" sura={2} aya="255" />

{/* layout and fontSize: per component */}
<QuranMadinaNative layout="IndoPak" sura={2} aya="255" />

// per widget on Android, iOS and macOS; on the web, the first widget's apply page-wide
QuranMadinaFlutter(layout: 'IndoPak', sura: 2, aya: '255')
1441H 1405H IndoPak Font DigitalKhatt New Madina DigitalKhatt Old Madina DigitalKhatt IndoPak Text Tanzil Uthmani, with the 1441H print's pause marks Tanzil Uthmani DigitalKhatt's IndoPak text (IndoPak spelling) Line breaks the 1441H print (King Fahd Complex page data) the 1405H print DigitalKhatt's IndoPak layout Pages 604 604 610

The value is not case sensitive. An unknown value logs a warning and falls back to 1441H.

docs.title: How lines are justified
docs.text:
Lines are filled the way the print fills them: by stretching the letters themselves, with kashida strokes and wider letter forms, rather than adding tatweel characters or squashing whole lines. Words keep the print's gaps between them; loose lines stretch letters, and dense lines narrow their words slightly (never the verse numbers). The text stays real text.

This uses the DigitalKhatt fonts by Amine Anane. The stretch of every word is decided when the databases are built, so the browser only needs the font. The design notes explain how it was measured against the print.

docs.title: Any size
docs.text:
data-font-size sets the size in pixels (default 16; anything from 6 to 100, decimals allowed). The whole page scales with it, line width included:

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2" data-font-size="24"></script>

{/* layout and fontSize apply to the whole page: set them on the first component */}
<QuranMadinaHtml fontSize={24} sura={2} aya="255" />

{/* layout and fontSize: per component */}
<QuranMadinaNative fontSize={24} sura={2} aya="255" />

// per widget on Android, iOS and macOS; on the web, the first widget's apply page-wide
QuranMadinaFlutter(fontSize: 24, sura: 2, aya: '255')

docs.title: Emphasising letters
docs.text:
letters colours single letters inside words, with a soft halo, for teaching a letter or pointing at a mistake. Nothing moves or changes size.

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="2-4" highlight="1" error="4"
  letters="1:3, 4:3+5 lapis blink, 6:4 emerald"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml
  sura={1}
  aya="2-4"
  highlight="1"
  error="4"
  letters="1:3, 4:3+5 lapis blink, 6:4 emerald"
/>

<QuranMadinaNative
  sura={1}
  aya="2-4"
  highlight="1"
  error="4"
  letters="1:3, 4:3+5 lapis blink, 6:4 emerald"
/>

QuranMadinaFlutter(
  sura: 1,
  aya: '2-4',
  highlight: '1',
  error: '4',
  letters: '1:3, 4:3+5 lapis blink, 6:4 emerald',
)

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
A comma-separated list of groups, each word:letters, then an optional colour, then an optional blink:

Part Values word a word number, counted like highlight letters 3 (one letter), 3-5 (letters 3 to 5) or 3+5 (letters 3 and 5) colour crimson (default), emerald, lapis, gold, violet, or any CSS colour blink makes the halo pulse gently; no animation without it

Examples: 1:3, 4:2-3 emerald, 6:1+4 #8a2be2 blink.

docs.title: How it looks
docs.text:
• The letter takes the colour, with a halo of the same colour that sits behind the surrounding ink, never over it.
  • With blink, only the halo pulses. The letter keeps its colour in every frame, so a screenshot always shows it. Blinking stops when printing and when the reader's system asks for reduced motion.
  • It works inside highlight and error words, and gets a lighter shade on dark pages.

docs.title: What counts as a letter
docs.text: Letters are counted as written. Diacritics and other marks, and tatweel, belong to the letter before them. Lam-alef (لا) is drawn as one shape, so marking either of its two letters colours both.

docs.title: A full page
docs.text:
page renders a whole Mushaf page, 1 to 604 (IndoPak: 1 to 610):

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html page="1"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml page={1} />

<QuranMadinaNative page={1} />

QuranMadinaFlutter(page: 1)

docs.title: A verse or a range
docs.text:
sura (1 to 114) and aya (one number, or a range like 8-10) render just those verses, laid out exactly as they sit on the page:

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="2" aya="8-10"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={2} aya="8-10" />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={2} aya="8-10" />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 2, aya: '8-10')

Verses are numbered the Kufan way in every layout, so the same sura and aya show the same verse whichever print you choose. A range may run onto the next page.

docs.title: Header or no header
docs.text:
A multiline render has a header with the sura name and two buttons: copy the text, and open the translation on quran.com. headless="true" keeps only the Quran text:

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="5" aya="1-2" headless="true"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={5} aya="1-2" headless />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={5} aya="1-2" headless />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 5, aya: '1-2', headless: true)

Clicking a verse opens a small copy/translate menu for that verse alone. It works on inline renders too, which have no header.

docs.title: Inline renders
docs.text:
A selection that fits on one line renders inline, inside the surrounding text, between quote marks: .

  • quotes="no" drops the quote marks.
  • inline="no" forces the multiline layout, with its header, even for a short selection.
HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="2" quotes="no"></quran-madina-html>
<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="2" inline="no"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya="2" quotes="no" />
<QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya="2" inline="no" />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya="2" quotes="no" />
<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya="2" inline="no" />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '2', quotes: 'no'),
QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '2', inline: 'no'),

docs.title: Self-hosting and offline
docs.text: By default the script and everything it loads come from unpkg. You can serve them yourself, from your own server or from inside an app, so pages render without unpkg or without any internet connection.

docs.title: What to serve
docs.text:
From the npm package (npm install quran-madina-html), keep this folder structure:

Path What dist/quran-madina-html.js the script dist/quran-madina-html.css its styles (loaded by the script) assets/img/ the sura frame assets/db/v2/<stem>/ the text and layout of one print, split per juz' assets/db/v2/<font>-qmh.woff2 that print's font

Through version 2.x, dist/ also holds the same two files under their old names, quran-madina-html.min.js and .min.css, so pages that link those keep working. Use the names above; the old ones go in 3.0.

The stems and fonts by layout:

Layout Database folder Font 1441H Madina-1441H/ madina-qmh.woff2 1405H Madina-1405H/ oldmadina-qmh.woff2 IndoPak IndoPak-15/ indopak-qmh.woff2

Each print takes about 4 MB. Serve only the ones you use.

docs.title: Point the script at your copy
docs.text:
data-cdn is the base URL that holds dist/ and assets/:

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<script src="/static/qmh/dist/quran-madina-html.js" data-cdn="/static/qmh/"></script>

{/* src, cdn and bundled apply to the whole page: set them on the first component */}
<QuranMadinaHtml page={1} src="/static/qmh/dist/quran-madina-html.js" cdn="/static/qmh/" />
{/* or offline, from the app's own copy (npx quran-madina-bundle; see React: Offline) */}
<QuranMadinaHtml page={1} bundled />

{/* from your own server */}
<QuranMadinaNative page={1} src="https://example.com/qmh/dist/quran-madina-html.js" cdn="https://example.com/qmh/" />
{/* or offline, from the app's own copy (npx quran-madina-native-bundle; see React Native: Offline) */}
<QuranMadinaNative page={1} bundled />

// from your own server
QuranMadinaFlutter(
  page: 1,
  src: 'https://example.com/qmh/dist/quran-madina-html.js',
  cdn: 'https://example.com/qmh/',
)
// or offline, from the app's own assets (see Flutter: online or offline)
QuranMadinaFlutter(page: 1, bundled: true)

Everything, the font included, then loads from there.

docs.title: The localhost rule
docs.text: Without data-cdn, the script loads its files from unpkg, except on a page served from localhost, where it assumes the files are one folder up (../). That is how this repository's own demo works locally. A dev server or an app shell that also runs on localhost (a React dev server, Capacitor) does not have the files there, so set data-cdn in those cases. The React and Flutter wrappers do it for you.

docs.title: Apps
docs.text:
• React (web, or iOS and Android with Capacitor): one command copies the files into public/. See React.
  • React Native: one command copies the files into the Android and iOS projects. See React Native.
  • Flutter: one command copies the files into the app's assets. See Flutter.

docs.title: Text colour
docs.text:
The text takes the colour of the surrounding page, like any text. To change it:

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
quran-madina-html { color: #3b2f2f; }

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={2} aya="255" style={{ color: "#3b2f2f" }} />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={2} aya="255" textColor="#3b2f2f" backgroundColor="#fdf8ee" />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 2, aya: '255', textColor: '#3b2f2f', backgroundColor: '#fdf8ee')

The CSS below applies to HTML and React pages. A React Native component's or Flutter widget's text sits in its own page: set textColor and backgroundColor instead; highlight, error and letter colours adapt to them.

docs.title: Colours you can change
docs.text:
Set these CSS custom properties on quran-madina-html, for all tags or for one:

Property Default Used for --qmh-background #F5F5DC the frame's tint (shown at 10%) --qmh-header black the header bar's tint --qmh-highlight #fff3b0 highlight background --qmh-highlight-text #1a1a1a highlight text --qmh-error #f5c6cb error background --qmh-error-text #1a1a1a error text --qmh-letter #a3263a default letters colour 
quran-madina-html {
  --qmh-highlight: #d7f5dd;
  --qmh-error: #ffd8a8;
}

Change colours only, never padding, margins or borders on the word spans: each word's width is part of the line's justification.

docs.title: Dark pages
docs.text:
The library checks the tag's actual text colour. When it is light (a dark page), it switches the highlight and error pairs to darker backgrounds with white text, and gives emphasised letters a lighter shade. This follows your page's own colours, however your dark mode is built (a class toggle, a theme, or the system setting), so there is nothing to configure.

The tag carries data-qmh-text-scheme="dark" or "light", which you can use in your own CSS:

quran-madina-html[data-qmh-text-scheme="dark"] { --qmh-highlight: #4a3b00; }

The check runs when a tag renders. If your page switches between light and dark without reloading, re-render the tags afterwards: setting any attribute again does it.

document.querySelectorAll("quran-madina-html").forEach(tag => {
  const key = tag.hasAttribute("page") ? "page" : "sura";
  tag.setAttribute(key, tag.getAttribute(key));
});

These docs do that: switch to dark mode (the moon icon in the header) to see the examples change.

docs.title: Printing and screenshots
docs.text:
• highlight and error backgrounds print, even where the browser skips backgrounds by default.
  • Blinking letters stop blinking when printed, and keep their colour in every frame for screenshots.

docs.title: CSS classes
docs.text: The generated elements have stable class names you can style; see CSS reference.

docs.title: Selecting words
docs.text:
words shows only some words, counted from the start of the given verse. The rest of the text stays in place but invisible, so the line keeps exactly the shape it has in the print.

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="1" words="1:2"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya="1" words="1:2" />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya="1" words="1:2" />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '1', words: '1:2')

docs.title: Range format
docs.text:
Words are numbered from 1, and both ends are included:

Value Means 5 word 5 only 3-10 or 3:10 words 3 to 10

Verse-number ornaments are not counted. words works with sura and aya; it is ignored on a full page. With an aya range, only the first verse sets where counting starts.

docs.title: Across verses, pages and suras
docs.text:
Counting carries on past the end of the verse, so a selection can cross verses, pages and even suras. After An-Nas it wraps around to Al-Fatiha.

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<!-- Al-Fatiha's last verse (9 words), Al-Baqara's basmala (4 words), then الٓمٓ -->
<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="7" words="1-14"></quran-madina-html>

{/* Al-Fatiha's last verse (9 words), Al-Baqara's basmala (4 words), then الٓمٓ */}
<QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya="7" words="1-14" />

{/* Al-Fatiha's last verse (9 words), Al-Baqara's basmala (4 words), then الٓمٓ */}
<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya="7" words="1-14" />

// Al-Fatiha's last verse (9 words), Al-Baqara's basmala (4 words), then الٓمٓ
QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '7', words: '1-14')

docs.title: The basmala counts as four words
docs.text:
The basmala at the top of a sura counts as its four words, matching the flat word numbering of the Tanzil text that most apps count with. This holds when a selection crosses into a new sura, and when it starts at a sura's first verse: word 1 is then بسم and word 5 is the verse's first word.

  • When all four words are selected, they show as the ﷽ ligature, as in the print. A partial selection shows the separate words. Either way the basmala takes four word numbers.
  • At-Tawba has no basmala, so it adds no words. Al-Fatiha's basmala is its real first verse.
  • The sura name above it is decoration and is never counted.

docs.title: Hiding the sura name
docs.text:
When you show a selection inside your own layout (a quiz that already names the sura, say), notitle="true" hides the name of a sura the selection crosses into. Its decorated frame stays, empty, and the basmala still shows:

HTMLReactReact NativeFlutter 
<quran-madina-html sura="1" aya="7" words="1-14" notitle="true"></quran-madina-html>

<QuranMadinaHtml sura={1} aya="7" words="1-14" notitle />

<QuranMadinaNative sura={1} aya="7" words="1-14" notitle />

QuranMadinaFlutter(sura: 1, aya: '7', words: '1-14', notitle: true)

docs.title: Limits and errors
docs.text:
• A selection is capped at 500 words.
  • A malformed or reversed range (10-3, 0) is ignored with a console message, and the verse renders whole.

Changes in older versions

  • 0.9.0: the basmala started counting as four words (before, it was never counted).
  • 0.9.3: a selection starting at a sura's first verse counts that sura's own basmala.
  • 0.9.5: a selection running past An-Nas wraps around to Al-Fatiha instead of stopping.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Everything you can set, in one place:

  • Tag attributes: what goes on each <quran-madina-html> tag.
  • Script options: what goes on the <script> tag, for the whole page.
  • CSS: custom properties, classes and generated elements.

docs.title: Tag attributes
docs.text:
Attributes of <quran-madina-html>. Changing one after the page loads re-renders the tag. Each is also a property: tag.aya = 256 sets aya="256" (from 2.1.2).

Attribute Value Default Description page 1–604 (IndoPak 1–610) A full Mushaf page. Takes priority over sura/aya. Guide sura 1–114 The sura, with aya. aya 255 or 8-10 A verse or a range of verses. Guide words 5, 3-10 or 3:10 Show only these words, counted from the start of aya. Ignored with page. Guide highlight a word range Mark words soft yellow. Works with page too. Guide error a word range Mark words soft red. Wins over highlight. Guide letters "1:3, 4:3-5 emerald blink" Colour single letters inside words. Guide headless true off Drop the header (sura name, copy and translate). notitle true off With words: hide the name of a sura the selection crosses into, keeping its frame. quotes no quote marks Drop the quote marks around an inline render. inline no auto Force the multiline layout even when the selection fits on one line.

Word ranges are 1-based and include both ends. A malformed words value is ignored and the verse renders whole; a malformed or out-of-range highlight, error or letters value is ignored on its own. Each logs a console message.

docs.title: Custom properties
docs.text:
Set on quran-madina-html. See Styling and dark mode for examples.

Property Default Dark page Used for --qmh-background #F5F5DC the frame's tint (10%) --qmh-header black the header bar's tint --qmh-highlight #fff3b0 #5c4600 highlight background --qmh-highlight-text #1a1a1a #ffffff highlight text --qmh-error #f5c6cb #6b1a24 error background --qmh-error-text #1a1a1a #ffffff error text --qmh-letter #a3263a lighter shade letters colour (set per group from the attribute)

docs.title: Generated elements and classes
docs.text:
Element or class What it is quran-madina-html-header the header bar (sura name, copy, translate) quran-madina-html-line one line of text quran-madina-html-aya-popup the copy/translate menu opened by clicking a verse .quran-madina-html-NNN-NNN the parts of one verse (sura and verse, three digits each), e.g. .quran-madina-html-002-255 .quran-madina-html-inline on the tag when it renders inline with quote marks .quran-madina-html-word-hidden a word outside a words selection (invisible, kept in place) .quran-madina-html-word-highlight a highlight word .quran-madina-html-word-error an error word .quran-madina-html-letter an emphasised letter .quran-madina-html-letter-blink an emphasised letter that blinks [data-qmh-text-scheme="dark"] on the tag when its text colour is light (a dark page)

Warning

Style colours only. Padding, margins, borders or a different font size on the words or lines would break the justification, which is computed from each word's width.

docs.title: Script options
docs.text:
Attributes of the <script> tag that loads the library. They apply to every tag on the page.

<script src="https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2"
        data-layout="1441H" data-font-size="16"></script>
Attribute Value Default Description data-layout 1441H, 1405H, IndoPak 1441H Which print. Not case sensitive; unknown values fall back to 1441H. Guide data-font-size 6–100 (px) 16 Size of the text. Decimals allowed. data-cdn a URL ending in / unpkg Where the CSS, databases and fonts load from. Guide data-font, data-name 1.x options, ignored since 2.0 with a console warning.

docs.title: Versions on unpkg
docs.text: src Loads https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2 the latest 2.x (recommended) https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@2.1.0 exactly 2.1.0 https://unpkg.com/quran-madina-html@1 the 1.x renderer (its docs)

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
1441H (default) 1405H (option) IndoPak 15-line (option) Font DigitalKhatt New Madina (hb/madina.otf) DigitalKhatt Old Madina (hb/oldmadina.otf) DigitalKhatt IndoPak (hb/indopak.otf) License OFL 1.1, no Reserved Font Name OFL 1.1, no Reserved Font Name OFL 1.1, no Reserved Font Name Line breaks KFGQPC 1441H print (src/db/v2/data/print-1441H-lines.json, see below) DigitalKhatt quran_text_old_madinah.ts (MIT); same breaks as the v1 Madina05 DB DigitalKhatt quran_text_indopak_15.ts (MIT) Line width 16200 font units 16400 font units 16400 font units

IndoPak was added at the user's request; its text and pause marks will need their own check against Tanzil (IndoPak spelling conventions differ).

The two layouts break lines differently on ~37% of lines (5658 of 9046 lines have the same word count).

docs.title: Text: Tanzil is the source
docs.text:
Tanzil stays the authoritative text. The DigitalKhatt texts are used only for line breaks. Tanzil words are converted at build time to the encoding the fonts expect (src/db/v2/tanzil_encoding.py): decomposed hamza with U+034F, no tatweel before dagger alef, ى → ي where it carries a vowel or follows kasra, ۝ + digits for aya numbers, ۞/۩ attached to their word, and the open tanween ࣰ ࣱ ࣲ derived by the tajweed rule (open before idgham/ikhfa letters, stacked before throat letters and hamzat wasl, plain vowel before the iqlab meem).

Checked over the whole Quran (src/db/v2/validate_encoding.py):

Reference Identical tokens Pause marks only Other 1405H text 84,112 / 84,116 1 3 (DigitalKhatt spacing quirks around ۞ ۩, v1 bug below) 1441H text 83,764 / 84,116 352 1 (v1 bug below)
  • Every letter of Tanzil matches both prints. The 1441H print revised 352 pause marks (waqf); Tanzil keeps the earlier ones. Decision: the 1441H layout uses the 1441H print's pause marks (tanzil_encoding.apply_pause_marks, aligned on text without marks; letters and vowels always stay Tanzil's). Result: 84,116 / 84,116 tokens identical.
  • v1 bug found: page 254 (13:37) — the v1 DB has no ﴿٣٧﴾ marker and puts "مَا" on line 7 instead of line 6.

docs.title: Stretching letters in browser text: position features in the font
docs.text:
Per-letter stretching (DigitalKhatt's cv01/cv02/cv10–cv18) cannot be done with nested spans: joining breaks (img/page3-per-letter-spans-broken.png), and even with ZWJ at span edges kerning and cursive attachment are lost (words drift up to 12px at 40px).

So the fonts are extended (src/db/v2/font_patch.py):

  1. At build time HarfBuzz justifies each line with per-letter features (justify.justify_line), exactly like DigitalKhatt's own justifier.
  2. Stretching never changes a word's glyph count (verified on all 19,482 stretched words of 1441H and 25,204 of 1405H), so each stretched word is recorded as "glyph at position k becomes glyph g′".
  3. The font gets one AlternateSubst lookup (g → its stretched variants) and features jp01…jpNN: jpKK swaps the glyph at position KK of the word, the CSS value picking the variant. These lookups run after all others, so GPOS (kerning, cursive, marks) sees exactly HarfBuzz's glyphs.
  4. Each word is one span: <span style='font-feature-settings: "jp04" 3'>…</span> (since the CoreText finding below, written "q043": an on/off twin of the same feature).

Results (Chromium, 40px): every word within 0.015px of HarfBuzz, every line within 0.08px of its target, on 1441H pages 3, 50, 300 and 1405H page 3. See img/1441h-page3-jp-chromium.png.

The patched fonts are renamed (OFL good practice) and rebuilt with the DB, since the alternate lists depend on the corpus.

docs.title: Open
docs.text:
• Firefox (not installable in this workspace): untested; it shapes with HarfBuzz, like Chrome.
  • Safari/CoreText (iOS 18, measured with demo/diag.html): custom features work, but CoreText ignores a feature's value in the nested AlternateSubst and always takes alternate 1, so stretched words came out up to 0.76em off. Fixed by giving the font one on/off feature per (position, alternate) pair (q043 = jp04 value 3); the runtime emits those everywhere. Afterwards every stretched word is within a pixel of Chrome. Left: two words with a kashida carrying hamza plus CGJ (لِـٔ͏َادَمَ +0.22em, يَٰٓـٔ͏َادَمُ −0.11em on page 6) still differ.
  • Pages 1-2, sura titles, basmala lines.

docs.title: Runtime (Phase 4)
docs.text:
<script src=".../quran-madina-html.js" data-layout="1441H"> (default 1441H, or 1405H) loads assets/db/v2/Madina-<layout>.json and its woff2 font. A page that sets data-font without data-layout keeps the v1 DBs.

  • Every v2 line gets its row from lines[page][line]: width (em), centering for titles/basmala/narrow lines, scaleX for the few shrunk lines.
  • Words are spans with their font-feature-settings; spaces are inline-block spans of the exact width. The words=, highlight=, error= and spacer paths all use the same builder (v2AppendWords), so selections keep the page geometry.
  • Copy/paste maps the font encoding back to standard Uthmani (CGJ removed, hamza recomposed, open tanween → regular).
  • No font-size anchors or interpolation: everything is in em.

Screenshot: img/v2-runtime-chromium.png (page 3, highlight/error, words=, inline quote, page 1).

Checked against the real Tanzil file (Uthmani 1.1, downloaded on 2026-10-16 without marks). Its letters and vowels match the text recovered from the v1 DB on every aya; the only difference is 17:7 لِيَسُـۥٓـُٔوا۟, where Tanzil puts a tatweel under the small waw (now handled by POST_CONVERSION). Built from that file, the 1441H DB is byte-identical to the committed one.

When the Tanzil text has no pause marks (marks=false), the builder takes the pause marks and the ۞ and ۩ signs from the layout's print text (they are not in the text itself either: ۞ 199, ۩ 15). For 1441H that changes nothing, since its pause marks come from the print anyway. For 1405H it differs in one place, 19:38 يَأْتُونَنَاۖ, where DigitalKhatt's 1405H text has no mark. The committed 1405H DB keeps Tanzil's mark; to rebuild it, download with marks: index.php?quranType=uthmani&outType=txt-2&marks=true&sajdah=true&rub=true&tatweel=true&agree=true.

docs.title: Matching the 1441H print (replaces the "hybrid" fitting)
docs.text:
The first v2 pages had overlapping words and crowded lines. Compared with the 1441H print (King Fahd Complex's own QCF4 data: one glyph per word, traced from the printed page, with the print's line breaks), three causes showed up:

  1. Line breaks. DigitalKhatt's "madina" text breaks 1,620 of 8,802 text lines differently from the 1441H print. 573 of its lines start with an aya number; the print never does that (0 lines). Lines that gain a word become overfull.
  2. shrr. This shrink feature overlaps letters: ٱلرِّقَابِ goes from 2351 to 1141 units. DigitalKhatt's own renderer never uses it. v2 had put it on 2,333 words.
  3. Squeezed spaces. On dense lines the print keeps its gaps and writes the words narrower (up to ~25%), and never touches aya numbers. v2 cut the spaces to 0.06 em, then scaled the whole line, aya numbers included.

The font size was not the cause: the DigitalKhatt font at z = 0.92 is close to the print (0.96 would match it exactly).

What changed:

  • Line breaks come from the print. extract_print_lines.py reduces the page data of the quran-qcf4 package (JSON: MIT) to the first and last token of each line, stored as sura:aya:index with the print's separate ۩ folded into its word. No glyphs or text are kept. Narrow lines (pages 1-2, some sura ends) take the print's width. The 1405H layout keeps DigitalKhatt's breaks, which already match the 1405H print.
  • Gaps follow the print. Gaps are measured ink to ink, band by band (ink.py: a word's leftmost and rightmost ink per 20-unit band), as a share of the line width. Values are from every 3rd page of the print:
gap p5 median p95 may move word / word 0.0058 0.0109 0.0181 0.55–1.65× word / ۝N 0.0095 0.0102 0.0201 0.93–1.9× ۝N / word 0.0078 0.0086 0.0097 0.91–1.13×

A space can be negative: the word boxes then overlap, but their ink never does. - Lines are fitted with the words (justify.fit_line_print): - Loose line: gaps open up to 1.2×, then letters stretch (DigitalKhatt's kashida and alternates, unchanged), then the gaps take the rest. - Dense line: gaps tighten within their range, then the words get narrower (c, a scaleX on each word span, down to 0.8, never on aya numbers). Only then is the whole line scaled (x). - shr1/shrr are no longer used.

1441H, every 10th page word pairs touching closest gaps (p1) word gaps median / p95 print 5 of 6,690 0.0050 0.0112 / 0.0188 v2 before 100 of 6,697 0.0000 0.0106 / 0.0281 v2 now 2 of 6,689 0.0056 0.0138 / 0.0181

"Touching" means within 1px at a 1600px line. 1441H now has 1,438 lines with narrowed words (277 below 0.9) and 20 line-scaled lines; 1405H has 885 and 7. test/v2_layout_test.py checks that every line has the print's words, that no line starts with an aya number, that no word uses shr*, and the closest gaps on sample pages.

docs.title: v2.0 — Phase 0 audit: DigitalKhatt New Madina
docs.text:
Goal of v2.0: replace build-time tatweel insertion with real glyph stretching (HarfBuzz shaping + the font's own stretch features), to look closer to the printed Madina Mushaf.

Update (Phase 1): the pilot font is now DigitalKhatt Old Madina, which matches our 1405H layout and has whole-word stretch features that work in the browser. See phase1-poc.md.

docs.title: Font first considered for the pilot
docs.text:
Font DigitalKhatt New Madina (hb/madina.otf, CFF2) Source github.com/DigitalKhatt/digitalkhatt.org @ 4213fab (2026-01-14), ClientApp/src/assets/fonts/hb/madina.otf Copyright © 2020-2024 Amine Anane, © 2024 Tarteel Inc. License SIL OFL 1.1 — fine to bundle in this repo/npm package (keep the license text next to it) Units/em 1000, 3735 glyphs

A sibling build, coretext/DigitalKhattV2.ttf (TrueType, 1219 glyphs, same OFL license), is published for Apple CoreText. It lacks cv01–cv18 and only offers jalt with fixed .expa alternates, so Safari will need a fallback.

docs.title: Not chosen
docs.text: digitalkhatt.otf ("DigitalKhatt Madina Quranic", V1) is the one with variable axes LTAT / RTAT (−20…20), which the TUGboat paper uses. It is AGPL-3.0 with a font-embedding exception, and its design follows the older layout. Usable for experiments, but a licensing question for an ISC library, so it is not the pilot font.

docs.title: Key finding: New Madina stretches through features, not axes
docs.text:
The New Madina font has no fvar table. Stretching is done with GSUB alternate lookups selected by an integer feature value:

Feature Role (observed) Max value cv01 kashida-like elongation of a joined letter pair 12 cv02 secondary elongation (finals / the left side) 12 cv03, cv10–cv18 single alternates (special forms) 1 jalt justification alternates (wide final forms) 1 shr1, shr2 / GPOS shrr shrinking —

Measured with uharfbuzz (font units, feature applied to the whole word):

Word natural cv01=2 cv01=4 cv01=6 cv02=6 cv02=12 ٱلْحَمْدُ 1755 2390 2928 3464 2495 3233 رَبِّ 1120 1360 1606 1853 1120 1120 ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ 2473 4222 5746 7144 3951 5430 لِلَّهِ 780 780 780 780 780 780

Takeaways: - Stretch is discrete but fine-grained (≈ 120–250 units per step), so lines can be fitted closely. - Applying a value to a whole word stretches every eligible pair and is not monotonic past some levels — values must target specific characters, as the reference algorithm does. - No .notdef for standard Uthmani Unicode text (Tanzil-style) in the samples.

docs.title: Reference algorithm (MIT)
docs.text: digitalkhatt.org (MIT license) ships a complete TypeScript justifier for this font: ClientApp/src/app/components/hbmedina/just.service.ts (~1.1k lines). It runs on HarfBuzz-WASM and outputs, per line, a map of character index → list of {feature, value}, using prioritized rules (final alternates, hah/kashida pairs, beh-beh, reh, kaf, then generic pairs) with level caps. That is exactly the shape a precomputed JSON DB needs. Plan: port it to Python in src/db/ instead of reinventing it.

docs.title: Current repo pipeline (v1.0.1) — what changes
docs.text:
• src/db/build_db.py measures widths in headless Chrome, computes per-line s (scaleX), and inserts tatweels (kashidas_needed / place_kashidas).
  • JSON contract: suras[].ayas[].r[] = {l, t, s}; runtime applies scaleX.
  • v2 adds a new, optional per-part field for feature runs; s remains as a small residual correction and as the v1 fallback.

docs.title: Risks confirmed
docs.text:
1. Safari/CoreText cannot use cv01/cv02 from the CoreText build → fallback (tatweel DB, or SVG paths) on WebKit.
  2. Per-character features in the browser: CSS font-feature-settings is per element. Applying it to a sub-word <span> may break Arabic joining in some engines. Must be tested in Chrome and Firefox before committing to the DOM approach (Phase 4). Fallback: HarfBuzz-WASM → SVG.
  3. Width parity: the build shapes with uharfbuzz, the browser shapes with its own HarfBuzz build; small differences are absorbed by the residual s.

docs.title: Decision: pilot font is DigitalKhatt Old Madina, not New Madina
docs.text:
The repo's layout is the 1405H Madina print (Madina05). DigitalKhatt ships a HarfBuzz build for exactly that layout:

Font DigitalKhatt Old Madina (ClientApp/src/assets/fonts/hb/oldmadina.otf, CFF2) License SIL OFL 1.1 — © 2023-2024 Amine Anane, © 2024 Tarteel Inc. Text DigitalKhatt quran_text_old_madinah.ts (MIT) — 604 pages × 15 lines, same line breaks as our DB (checked on pages 1-3) and the encoding the font expects (e.g. hamza written with U+034F joiners)

Besides the per-letter cv01–cv18 features (Phase 0), this font has whole-word stretch features: jt01–jt05, dc01–dc03, kt01–kt05. Switching one on for a word lets the font itself pick which letters to stretch.

docs.title: 1. Per-letter features in the DOM: rejected
docs.text: justify.justify_line() (port of DigitalKhatt's HarfBuzz justifier) sets cvNN values on single letters. Wrapping those letters in their own <span style="font-feature-settings: …"> breaks letter joining in Chromium (see img/page3-per-letter-spans-broken.png): كفر و، يؤ منون، عذابـ… Per-letter control can only be shown as SVG paths, not as browser text.

docs.title: 2. Per-word features in the DOM: works, pixel-exact
docs.text:
justify.justify_words() (port of DigitalKhatt's oldmedina DOM justifier) assigns jt/dc/kt levels per word, computed at build time with HarfBuzz. Each word is one span with one font-feature-settings, so joining is intact.

Chromium vs HarfBuzz, page 3, 15 lines at 40px:

  • every word's width matches within 0.015px
  • every line lands within 0.06px of the 656px target

Side by side with the real v1 runtime (Hafs, 24px): img/page3-v1-vs-v2-chromium.png.

docs.title: 3. Geometry
docs.text:
• Line width: 16400 font units (= the DigitalKhatt page width). Their site uses 15628, but then ~37% of lines are wider than the line and have to shrink. At 16400, page 3 needs no shrinking and spaces stay near normal.
  • Spaces may grow to 1.5× before letters stretch (space_stretch=0.5).
  • Lines wider than the target: spaces tighten to 60%, then the font's shr1/shrr features per word, then a residual scaleX (rare).

docs.title: Not covered yet
docs.text:
• Firefox: Playwright's Firefox download is blocked in this workspace, so only Chromium was measured. Firefox also shapes with HarfBuzz, so similar results are expected, but it must be checked.
  • Safari: CoreText ignores these custom features → fallback needed.
  • Pages 1-2 (narrow centered lines), sura headers, basmala lines.
  • Word count: the DigitalKhatt text joins some tokens differently from Tanzil (e.g. aya markers ۝١٣); word indexes must still match the words= API.

docs.text:
